memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If any of your people—Hebrew men or women—sell themselves to you and serve you six years, in the seventh year you must let them go free. And when you release them, do not send them away empty-handed. Supply them liberally from your flock, your threshing floor and your winepress. Give to them as the Lord your God has blessed you. - Deut 15:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In Israel, a person who had fallen into poverty might sell themselves into service to pay their debts. But God set a limit: after six years, they were to be set free. And He added something beautiful — they were not to be sent away "empty-handed." The one being released was to be supplied "liberally," given resources to start their new life well. Freedom was not to be a cruel abandonment but a generous new beginning, so the freed person could truly flourish.

This law reveals God's tender care for the vulnerable and His concern for genuine restoration, not just technical release. It would have been easy to free someone in name while leaving them destitute and likely to fall back into servitude. God guarded against this. He wanted the freed person to leave with dignity and provision, given a real chance at a fresh start. His concern was for their flourishing, not merely their legal status.

Notice the motive God gives: "Give to them as the Lord your God has blessed you." Our generosity flows from remembering how generously God has treated us. And this points to the gospel. We were slaves — slaves to sin — and Christ set us free (John 8:36). But He did not free us empty-handed. He lavished on us every spiritual blessing, forgiveness, His Spirit, adoption as children, an eternal inheritance (Eph 1:3-8). God's freedom is always generous. As we have been so richly blessed in our own release, we are called to bless others generously, giving them not just freedom but the means to flourish.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I give others not just release but the means to truly flourish?
- How has God set me free and blessed me generously in Christ?
- Whom might God be calling me to help toward a genuine fresh start?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You set me free from slavery to sin and did not leave me empty-handed, but lavished every blessing on me in Christ. Help me bless others as generously as You have blessed me, giving not just freedom but the means to flourish. Amen.
